Agency submission — Culture, escalation, and non‑retaliation (draft): We acknowledge to the Agency that Norbridge’s formal escalation channels, non‑retaliation policies, and related training infrastructure were in place for several years, and that our own reviews and subsequent investigations have produced three concurrent findings that we present here plainly: (a) confirmed facts — since 2019 we had written policies, multiple reporting channels (including anonymous reporting), and a documented, limited number of substantiated retaliation cases that resulted in corrective action; (b) recurring patterns still under reconstruction — internal audit cross‑checks, employee surveys, and regional case reviews show that in some facilities and regions employees felt pressure or hesitation to escalate safety and quality concerns, and our earlier external language tended to understate the breadth of issues those internal reports described; and (c) our remedial and governance actions to date — over the past 12–18 months we have tightened reporting protocols (standardized escalation thresholds and timelines), launched targeted retraining, implemented enhanced protections for reporters (including expanded confidentiality safeguards and an independent intake option), initiated a company‑wide review of past escalation decisions, and, where investigations substantiated misconduct, taken disciplinary steps; we are commissioning an independent third‑party review to examine culture and retaliation risk across affected sites, will provide the Agency with its scope and independent reviewer selection, and commit to regular written updates on findings and remediation progress while preserving confidentiality for ongoing investigations and complying with privilege and legal obligations.

All‑employee email suggested edits (bite‑sized, plain language): I understand recent reporting and the Agency’s hearing have raised real concern and pain for many of you — we take those concerns seriously; we have policies and reporting channels to protect people who raise safety or quality issues, but our reviews show that in some places those systems did not work as intended and that some employees felt pressured or discouraged from speaking up; we are therefore expanding protections now — including an independent third‑party review of escalation practices, strengthened confidentiality and anonymous reporting options, clearer escalation timelines, retraining for managers and teams, and faster follow‑up for reported concerns — and we will communicate regularly about what we learn and the corrective actions we take; if you have concerns or believe you experienced retaliation, please contact HR or the independent intake (details below) and we will ensure your report is handled confidentially and promptly; leadership is committed to hearing and addressing failures and protecting employees who raise issues in good faith.

Public statement for The Chronicle and website (draft): We recognize the seriousness of the whistleblower account published today and the related questions about whether our culture and escalation practices have allowed safety and quality concerns to go insufficiently addressed; our internal audits and board briefings over recent years show recurring deficiencies and, as we have previously acknowledged, our public descriptions at times did not fully reflect the scope of those internal findings — that gap between internal reports and external language is unacceptable and we are confronting it directly. We have taken tangible steps to improve conditions where problems were identified, including targeted remediation at higher‑risk sites, strengthened reporting protections, and an independent review of our culture and escalation practices; we are also cooperating fully with the Agency’s inquiry and will provide the Agency and the public a published scope for the independent review and a regular reporting cadence for remediation progress. We will not speculate about individual motives or unresolved personnel matters here; instead, we will make verifiable findings and corrective actions public as they are completed, and we ask for the time necessary to do that work thoroughly and transparently.
